title: Directional scopaesthesia paper from almost a thousand case histories

tellings.quote: my most recent paper on the subject is called directional scalesia and its implications for theories of and by examining almost a thousand case histories of people responding to being looked at

plain: A scientist, Rupert Sheldrake, studies scopaesthesia, the feeling of being stared at. He says his most recent paper on it, called Directional Scopaesthesia and its Implications for Theories of Vision, looked at almost a thousand case histories of people reacting to being looked at. He presents it as saying something about how seeing itself works, which would matter a great deal if the effect is real.
